findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false with inverted dead logic
findings.body: In pkg/expr/reader.go enableSqlExpressions computes enabled as !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions) and then returns false in both the if-branch and the fall-through, so it always denies. The negation is backwards and the branch is dead code. The intent to unconditionally disable SQL is achieved, but the confusing logic invites a future cleanup to return enabled, which would silently re-enable DuckDB SQL expressions and reintroduce the CVE-2024-9264 RCE/LFI. Simplify to an unconditional return false with a comment explaining the intentional security disable.

findings.title: Legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path not explicitly disabled
findings.body: In pkg/expr/sql_command.go UnmarshalSQLCommand parses the expression and calls NewSQLCommand with no disabled check, while pkg/expr/reader.go ReadQuery explicitly rejects QueryTypeSQL. The legacy rawNode path is therefore only blocked incidentally because the stubbed sql.TablesList always returns not implemented. Relying on incidental DB failure instead of an explicit deny means restoring a real DB implementation or changing error handling silently re-exposes DuckDB execution and the RCE/LFI vulnerability. Both entry points must explicitly reject SQL expressions.

findings.title: TablesList still attempts DuckDB json_serialize_sql instead of hard-failing
findings.body: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go TablesList still builds SELECT json_serialize_sql('...') with strings.Replace quote doubling and fmt.Sprintf and calls RunCommands. With the current stub it fails, but the vulnerable DuckDB-specific code path and injection-prone string interpolation are preserved. If the stub is ever replaced with a real DuckDB connection the RCE/LFI returns. TablesList should return an explicit disabled error immediately without constructing or executing any SQL.

findings.title: No regression test that SQL stays disabled regardless of flag
findings.body: In pkg/expr/reader.go the QueryTypeSQL case is now supposed to always fail, but the PR adds no automated test verifying rejection via ReadQuery and via the legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path with FlagSqlExpressions both on and off. Without a regression test a later refactor can accidentally re-enable DuckDB SQL execution and reintroduce RCE/LFI without detection. Add tests asserting an explicit disabled error in all flag states.
